title: B-ROLL: Coast Guard rescues 2 people from disabled sailboat near Daly City
description: A Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco MH-65 Dophin helicopter crew rescued two people after their sailboat became disabled two miles west of Daly City, Calif., Dec. 13, 2021. Lt. Jacob Schroeder, an Air Station San Francisco pilot, discusses the rescue. (U. S. Coast Guard courtesy b-roll video/Interview by Petty Officer 2nd Class Brandon Giles)
keywords: Air Station San Francisco, Daly City, Coast Guard, California, rescue

transcript.text: At around 6.05 in the evening, we received an initial report from
Sector San Francisco about a father and daughter who were stranded on a disabled sailing vessel
that were experiencing seasickness and were requesting an immediate extraction.
Winds were pretty strong out of the south, ripping out, and seas were a little bit heavy,
probably about 9 to 10 foot seas, but we were able to find the boat pretty easily.
So as soon as we located the vessel and confirmed that it was in fact the vessel that we were
supposed to be searching for, we immediately set them up by telling them exactly what we planned
on doing. We told them that we were going to plan on taking them both directly from the water
since their sailing vessel was an unstable hoist platform. So we went through and kind of guided
them through that process about what we were going to do, how we were going to send our swimmer down
initially to establish contact, and then he basically walked them through the remainder of the process
from there. We put him in the water, he got to the water safely, he swam a very short distance, maybe
only like 30 yards, was able to successfully get on top of the boat. Once he was there,
he established radio contact with us directly in the aircraft, told us exactly what he was going to
do. He's from that point on started to prepare the survivors for extraction, and the male
was the first person to go overboard with the rescue swimmer. They jumped in tandem into the
water, we lowered the rescue basket down, the survivor was placed in the rescue basket, and our swimmer
attached it himself via his harness to the hook as well, and we lifted them simultaneously from the
water. Because the boat made it to the surf show before we were actually able to send the swimmer back
down to get her. So she went on a little bit of a ride for probably about a minute or so, and
eventually the boat settled out and beached itself, and was pinned there by the waves. Fortunately,
the sand vessel had a heavy keel on it, so it kind of dug into the sand there. And so what we decided
to do at that point was for go any type of extract from the water, we were basically doing a land
hoist at that point, and we elected to do a harness to point of our rescue swimmer down to the beachhead,
and from there he simply just walked out, was able to direct the female out of the vessel safely,
recovered her and walked her away from the boat so it was no longer hazard to them, and then we
lowered the basket, brought her up in it, and then lowered the bear hoist hook down after that,
and picked the swimmer up. Based off of visible symptoms that we could see from
ourselves and after discussing with our rescue swimmer, we elected to take the father and the
daughter back to Air Station San Francisco directly where we had pre-coordinated the emergency medical
services to await our return. This case last night just drives home the importance of ensuring that
you have everything at your disposal, even if you don't think that a situation of a rise where you
would fall into trouble. So I would just highly recommend to the public and the general community
that you just take the appropriate action to ensure that you're prepared for anything that might come
up. Given the fact that we are currently in the Christmas season, this is safe and successful
extraction we did last night is much more meaningful to us knowing that we were able to safely return
these two members to their family, and we hope that they all have a happy and merry Christmas together.
